_about: The lint for forward-facing lines, from Orb's marks on the first ten (docs/ep/vision.md, 'Orb marks the first ten lines', 2026-10-15). Each rule is traced in docs/narrative/writing-quality.md section 0. Narrative's additions to the banned list are marked proposed: Orb may veto them.

R1_length.why: Orb's directive: Mid-Punch Brevity; marks 3 and 10

R3_banned_words.why: Orb's directive: Ban LLM Thesaurus Words

R4_physical_trigger.why: Orb's directive: physical, blue-collar words; a line reacts to what just happened

R5_no_dynamic_explained.why: Orb's directive: write for the English dub

R6_second_person.why: all ten of Orb's rewrites address the opponent

ellipsis.cap: at most one line in ten per fighter in any batch (at least one is allowed for a block under ten)
ellipsis.check_by_hand: whether the line really is hesitation, regret or performative exhaustion

R8_punctuation.why: Orb's rewrites 1, 4, 5 and Orb's note of 2026-10-15

R9_reference_lines.why: Orb: a style target, trimmed down and punchier

tells: a word or phrase said three times for feeling
a one-word zinger as the last sentence
the same joke device on every line of one fighter
a line that describes the blow or the mechanic
the opponent explained to the opponent (the dynamic said aloud)

stance: wants the rival at full strength
concerned when a launch heads at a crowd

c10_tiers._about: Legal c10 (docs/legal/homework8-review-screen.md). Whole-word matches, so 'bombardment' is not caught by 'bomb'. The same lists guard place names and every generated line.
c10_tiers._glass: Legal RL-153 to RL-155 (docs/legal/gemini-lines-screen.md): 'glass' as a verb for a bombed ground is the military idiom for nuclear destruction (c07's association). A human reads any line with it; 'burn' or 'flatten' are preferred. Place names such as Glassmere are not affected (whole-word match; the --names check lets 'glass' pass).

gemini_review_2026_10_16._about: Orb's homework 11 marks, run through Gemini at Orb's direction (docs/ep/vision.md, 2026-10-16 night). The lint runs these per speaker block (a '## ' heading containing the speaker's name). A heading containing '3v1' lifts the guard ban; a heading containing 'after the fight' lifts the apology ban.
gemini_review_2026_10_16.direct_address: A 1v1 line is aimed at the opponent: never at an object ('Sorry, shop!') or an off-screen minion ('Guard, write that down'). In 3v1 the Empress commands her guards.

cyborg_ln04_ln05._about: Legal ln04 and ln05 (docs/legal/beat-templates-screen.md): a Cyborg line never names people, a toll or a casualty. Whole-word match, hard fail, in any block whose heading names the Cyborg and in any JSON line whose speaker is the Cyborg. 'gone' and 'lost' are printed for a human to read (they fail when a people word is also in the line, which the hard list already catches).

orb_own_exemption.ruling: EP 2026-10-28: Orb's own words win. A line whose `source` is Orb's own is exempt from R1 (length) and R8 (the ellipsis rule, in a line and in a batch). Every other rule stays strict for it, and the lint stays strict for every other line.
orb_own_exemption.keyed_on: the line's `source` field (data), never a list of strings
orb_own_exemption.not_exempt: Orb's marks on lines others wrote (hw11: claude_kept_by_orb_hw11, ai01_gemini_rewrite_at_orb_direction_hw11) are not Orb's own words, so they stay strict. A line Orb writes carries source `orb`.
orb_own_exemption.applies_to: python docs/narrative/line-lint.py --live FILE.json (a data file whose beats hold lines with a source, such as data/narrative/live_barks.json). Markdown batches carry no source and are always strict.
